name: 7S Video & Music Gallery
author: durdagi

sections.description:
Give your video and music a place of its own

Video and music should feel like a real part of your website—not just embeds scattered between regular posts.

7S Video & Music Gallery turns WordPress into a focused media destination where visitors can discover, watch, listen, like, and share your content through a clean, responsive gallery.

Publish a video, soundtrack, performance, trailer, interview, playlist, or any other media entry from one familiar WordPress interface. The plugin creates the gallery, individual content pages, players, browsing tools, and interaction statistics for you.

A gallery designed for discovery

Welcome visitors with a cinematic featured area, guide them toward community favourites with Most Liked, and keep fresh content easy to explore through a clear media stream.

Live search responds as visitors type. Related content encourages them to continue browsing, while numbered pagination, Load More, and infinite scrolling let you choose how the experience flows.

Everything works together as one coherent media section rather than a collection of unrelated embeds.

Publish from the sources you already use

Add media from:

  • YouTube and YouTube Music
  • Vimeo
  • Spotify
  • Apple Music
  • SoundCloud
  • Deezer
  • Direct video and audio URLs
  • Your WordPress Media Library

Add a title, cover image, description, category, and supporting details, then publish it like any other WordPress content.

Make the gallery feel like part of your website

Use your theme’s typography or give the gallery its own visual identity. Adjust widths, typography, card titles, featured content, Most Liked presentation, colors, browsing behaviour, and individual content pages from a dedicated settings panel with live previews.

The gallery uses consistent 16:9 media presentation and adapts across desktop and mobile screens.

Turn visitor activity into useful insight

Visitors can like content without creating an account and remove their likes whenever they choose. Logged-in visitors’ preferences remain connected to their WordPress accounts.

The built-in Statistics screen shows:

  • Total and recent views
  • Total and recent likes
  • Most-viewed content
  • Most-liked content
  • Per-item interaction totals
  • Recent gallery activity

Statistics update while the screen is open, without sending analytics data to the plugin author or requiring a separate analytics service.

Built for creative and editorial websites

7S Video & Music Gallery is a natural fit for:

  • Film and culture publications
  • Music magazines and artist websites
  • Video archives and editorial projects
  • Portfolios and creative studios
  • Festivals, performances, and event media
  • Podcasts with supporting video or audio
  • Any WordPress site that wants media to feel like a destination

Everything in one WordPress workflow

  • Dedicated video and music archive
  • Individual media pages
  • Featured-content showcase
  • Thumbnail-based Most Liked section
  • Live gallery search
  • Related media
  • Reversible guest and member likes
  • View and like statistics
  • Social sharing controls
  • Flexible pagination options
  • Gallery-specific typography and appearance settings
  • ZIP import and export
  • Theme-independent responsive layouts

Your content stays in WordPress, your presentation remains under your control, and your media gains a space built specifically for watching, listening, and discovery.

External Services

7S Video & Music Gallery connects to an external service only when a site administrator publishes media from that service or a visitor chooses a sharing button. The plugin author does not receive this data.

Embedded players

When a supported media item is viewed, the visitor’s browser loads the player from the selected provider. That provider may process the media identifier, IP address, browser or device information, referrer data, and cookies under its own policies.

  • YouTube / YouTube Music: Privacy · Terms
  • Vimeo: Privacy · Terms
  • Spotify: Privacy · Terms
  • Apple Music: Privacy · Terms
  • SoundCloud: Privacy · Terms
  • Deezer: Privacy · Terms

Direct external media

Administrators may enter a direct video or audio URL hosted on another domain. The visitor’s browser connects to that administrator-selected host only when the media is viewed. The site owner is responsible for that host’s terms and privacy disclosures.

Optional sharing

Sharing links are created locally. The visitor connects to a service only after clicking its button, which sends the content URL and title; Pinterest may also receive the cover-image URL and description.

  • Facebook: Privacy · Terms
  • X: Privacy · Terms
  • WhatsApp: Privacy · Terms
  • Telegram: Privacy · Terms
  • LinkedIn: Privacy · Terms
  • Reddit: Privacy · Terms
  • Pinterest: Privacy · Terms

Privacy

7S Video & Music Gallery does not send analytics or usage data to the plugin author.

To reduce duplicate views, the plugin uses a first-party cookie for up to 24 hours and temporarily stores a one-way salted fingerprint for up to six hours. Raw IP addresses and raw browser identifiers are not stored.

Guest likes use a random first-party browser token for up to one year; only its one-way salted hash is saved. Logged-in visitors are represented by a one-way salted hash of their WordPress user ID. Raw identifiers and IP addresses are not stored with likes.

Third-party embedded players may process visitor data according to the policies listed in the External Services section.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate 7S Video & Music Gallery from WordPress.
  2. Open 7S Gallery > Settings and choose how your gallery should look and behave.
  3. Open 7S Gallery > Add New Media Content.
  4. Add a title and a media source, then publish.
  5. Add selected items to the Featured area if you want them highlighted at the top of the gallery.

If you change the gallery permalink settings, save the WordPress permalink settings once afterward.
sections.faq:
Is this a photo gallery plugin?

No. 7S Video & Music Gallery is focused on video, music, and audio content.

Which media services can I use?

YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, Deezer, direct video/audio URLs, and files from the WordPress Media Library are supported.

Do I need a featured image for every item?

No. If a cover image is not assigned, the plugin can create a 16:9 fallback cover for the content.

Can I choose what appears at the top of the gallery?

Yes. The Featured Items area lets you select and order highlighted content. You can also give the area your own title and set its title size independently.

Can visitors search the gallery?

Yes. The gallery includes live search and standard fallback navigation.

Can I choose how visitors browse more content?

Yes. You can use numbered pagination, a Load More button, or infinite scrolling.

Does the plugin include social sharing?

Yes. You can enable or disable the sharing tools and choose which supported platforms are shown on individual content pages.

Can visitors like content without an account?

Yes. Guests can like content without signing in and can remove their like from the same browser. Logged-in visitors’ likes are tied to their WordPress account.

Can I see which content is popular?

Yes. The gallery home page can show a most-liked index for the last 7 days, last 30 days, or all time. The Statistics area shows live view and like totals, recent activity, and the most popular video and audio content.

Will it work with my theme?

The plugin is designed to work with themes that follow standard WordPress practices. It also includes its own width, typography, and appearance controls when you want the gallery to have a more independent presentation.

Does uninstalling the plugin delete my content?

No. Published media content, taxonomies, view and like data, and Media Library files are preserved. Plugin settings and temporary transfer data are removed.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Expanded the Settings interface to the full available WordPress administration width and redesigned the white Typography preview with a spacious two-row layout, current gallery structures, and universal sample titles.
  • Added live like statistics for total, today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days, plus most-liked content and per-item like totals.
  • Added automatic five-second interaction refreshes while the Statistics screen is open.
  • Moved Import / Export from its own submenu into a dedicated Settings section while preserving old administration links through a compatibility redirect.
  • Reduced the empty space between the archive toolbar and the Most Liked section without changing later section spacing.
  • Added a Most Liked color picker for the filled heart icon.
  • Added media-type and view-count details below titles in the Most Liked list.
  • Increased the gallery menu, home, and search icons by one pixel for clearer visibility.
  • Removed unused showcase modifier hooks left behind by the former layout.
  • Reworked the showcase into one large 16:9 card beside four compact cards in a 2 × 2 group, with a matching mobile layout.
  • Added targeted LiteSpeed cache tagging and automatic gallery cache purging when settings change.
  • Rebuilt the gallery home page around a five-item showcase, a thumbnail-led popularity list, and a four-column media stream.
  • Added controls for the most-liked title, ranking period, item count, and visibility.
  • Added a one-to-four-column setting for the most-liked thumbnail list, with three columns as the default.
  • Added a configurable card-title character limit and kept archive titles to one line.
  • Replaced category text below cards with compact video or music icons inside the images.
  • Replaced ranking numbers in the most-liked area with small 16:9 content images.
  • Removed image overlays, metric pills, hover zoom, and heavy rounding from the archive experience.
  • Removed repeated separator lines between home-page sections and cards.
  • Removed the white border ring around the video and music icons inside card images.
  • Kept live-search transitions coherent by hiding home-only sections during a search and restoring the content-stream heading when results update.
  • Added reversible content likes for guests and logged-in visitors, including live counts on archive and featured cards.
  • Added a Single Content setting to enable or disable likes without deleting existing like data.
  • Pruned retired settings during upgrades.
  • Removed the technical archive prefix from the gallery browser title and plugin archive headings.
  • Removed the visible Loading player placeholder while keeping an accessible loading/error status.
  • Prevented Infinite Scroll background requests from fading the entire gallery, eliminating the brief white flash during scrolling.
  • Renamed the public-facing product to 7S Video & Music Gallery so its purpose is clear at a glance while keeping the existing 7sgaleri slug, text domain, directory, and sg7g technical identifiers for compatibility.
  • Rewrote the WordPress.org description around real publishing use cases instead of implementation details.
  • Removed the obsolete direct sharing renderer left from the former template-integration path.
  • Removed the pre-WordPress.org sg7-to-sg7g private-build migration and its unused migration flag.
  • Removed the obsolete v1 administration badges, leftover eyebrow labels, and their unused constant/styles.
  • Removed an unused single-cover CSS selector and a duplicated visually-hidden utility block.
  • Removed social-network names and external sharing URLs from the front-end button DOM; share destinations are now created only after a visitor clicks a sharing control.
  • Rebuilt all social share actions as button controls and fixed sharing initialization when Copy Link is disabled.
  • Hardened sharing setting persistence and legacy truthy-value handling.
  • Moved social sharing controls and platform selection into Single Content settings.
  • Added a custom Featured area title with an independent, uncapped font-size control.

1.1.0

  • Renamed the public-facing plugin brand from 7SGaleri to 7SGallery.
  • Kept the existing 7sgaleri plugin slug, text domain, directory name, and sg7g technical identifiers for update and backward compatibility.

1.0.1

  • Fixed front-end asset cache compatibility after the directory-safe prefix migration.
  • Added cache-busting asset versions and aligned all public selectors with the sg7g prefix.

1.0.0

  • Initial stable WordPress.org release.
  • Added dedicated video and audio content, featured layouts, search, pagination, statistics, sharing, import/export, and translation-ready strings.
